findings.severityNote: Residual of ledger High 1c222d548523 (fix-pending). This is an INCOMPLETE-FIX signal, not a regression. Do NOT auto-flip 1c222d548523 to `fixed`. Final rank belongs to severity-classifier adjudicating against the H-01 entry; the migrator-side mechanism itself is verified correct, so the residual is narrower than the original High.
findings.specText: story-023 (commit f3b92c0 body): "NFTStakerDepletion.depositFor settles the incoming user's pending phUSD with _safePay(pending), which pays msg.sender -- the migrator -- instead of the user. That staker is deployed and immutable, so the remediation lands on the migrator side." ... "NO staker contract is modified."
findings.actualBehavior: src/NFTStakerDepletion.sol:756 still reads `pending = _safePay(pending);` at HEAD, and :757 still emits `Claimed(user, pending)`. The root cause is untouched. The compensating control exists only inside two source files (src/NFTStakerMigrator.sol:214-241, src/InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.sol:311-338) and therefore only binds callers that are (a) contracts, (b) compiled from post-f3b92c0 source, and (c) currently wired via setMigrator.
findings.deviation: The story's stated justification for declining a source fix -- 'that staker is deployed and immutable' -- is true of existing instances but not of the file. src/NFTStakerDepletion.sol is the LIVE DEPLOYMENT TEMPLATE: lib/phoenix-phase-2-staging/script/DeployMainnetUniboostCutover.s.sol:478 executes `new NFTStakerDepletion(...)` and deployed three fresh mainnet instances (EYE/SCX/FLX) under phStaging story-071, and lib/phoenix-phase-2-staging/script/DeployMocks.s.sol:1461-1472 deploys more. Every instance deployed after story-023 still carries the defect. Four residual reach-paths survive the migrator-side remedy: (1) DIRECT EOA/MULTISIG CALLER -- depositFor is `onlyMigrator`, and src/NFTStakerDepletion.sol:311-314 `setMigrator` accepts ANY address with no code-size check and no lifecycle gate, so an operator address wired as migrator reaches depositFor directly and receives the user's settlement with `Claimed(user, ...)` still emitted; (2) ANY PRE-f3b92c0 MIGRATOR INSTANCE already deployed and wired -- the fix lands only on redeploy, and the commit body never states the deployment prerequisite (redeploy both orchestrators AND re-run setMigrator on both stakers); (3) ANY FUTURE THIRD ORCHESTRATOR (see F-21-02); (4) EVERY FUTURE NFTStakerDepletion DEPLOYMENT. The correct form already exists in-tree at src/NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady.sol:887 (`_safePayTo(user, pending)`), whose own NatSpec at :869-876 calls the `_safePay` form 'wrong in every case' -- so the repo simultaneously documents the pattern as wrong and ships it as the deployment template.
findings.recommendation: Fix src/NFTStakerDepletion.sol:756 to `_safePayTo(user, pending)` for FUTURE instances (zero cost, matches the in-tree correct sibling) and keep the migrator-side forwarding as the compensating control for the three already-deployed instances. Additionally: document the deployment prerequisite in the story (redeploy both migrators + setMigrator on both stakers) and consider a code-size check in setMigrator.

findings.specText: story-023: "NEW src/IStakerViews.sol: local rewardToken()/pendingReward(address) extension; INFTStakerMigratable is deliberately left unwidened (D-5)." and src/NFTStakerMigrator.sol:204-205: "line-for-line identical to InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator's (plan decision D-6 -- a divergence here is exactly the fork drift that produced pns20h1)."
findings.specSource: git commit f3b92c0 body; src/NFTStakerMigrator.sol:202-205; src/IStakerViews.sol:11-19
findings.actualBehavior: src/INFTStakerMigratable.sol:40-46 documents depositFor as 'Permissioned deposit crediting `user` with `amount` ERC1155 units pulled from the caller (the migrator)' with no mention that the target staker may settle the user's pending reward to msg.sender. D-5 deliberately declined to widen the interface, and the warning about the misroute lives only in src/NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady.sol:869-876 -- a file a new orchestrator author has no reason to open.
findings.deviation: The story names fork drift as the root cause it is defending against, but leaves the one artifact that defines the migrator role -- the shared interface -- completely silent about the trap. A fourth orchestrator written against INFTStakerMigratable alone reproduces pns20h1 exactly, with no compile-time, interface-level, or NatSpec signal. D-5's rationale ('purely a migrator-local concern') is sound for the type system but not for the hazard disclosure.
findings.recommendation: Leave the interface unwidened per D-5, but add a `@dev` warning block to INFTStakerMigratable.depositFor stating that some implementations settle to msg.sender and that any orchestrator MUST implement the capture-and-forward sequence.

findings.specText: src/NFTStakerMigrator.sol:48-50: "Against a correct staker the measured capture is ZERO and no transfer occurs, so the branch is self-disabling and this contract is version-agnostic across every staker exposing `depositFor`." Commit body: "which is what makes one migrator codebase version-agnostic."
findings.actualBehavior: The forwarding sequence requires THREE getters on the target, not one: `depositFor` (INFTStakerMigratable), `rewardToken()` and `pendingReward(address)` (src/IStakerViews.sol:26,30). The constructor validates `rewardToken()` on both stakers (src/NFTStakerMigrator.sol:133-140; InPlace at :167-170) but NEVER probes `pendingReward`. A staker exposing depositFor + rewardToken() but not pendingReward(address) constructs successfully and then reverts on the FIRST migrate/migrateIn call at src/NFTStakerMigrator.sol:215 / src/InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.sol:312.
findings.deviation: The 'version-agnostic across every staker exposing depositFor' claim is over-stated by exactly one unvalidated getter. The failure is discovered at the worst moment: `initiateMigration` (src/NFTStakerDepletion.sol:653-660) has already flipped the pool to Migrating and frozen emissions, and for the in-place path the ERC1155 is already parked, so recovery is claimTimedOut (stake only, no re-accrual, no automatic re-entry) after MIN_TIMEOUT = 1 days. Non-obvious deploy-time footgun (Law 3, in scope).
findings.recommendation: Add a constructor staticcall probe of `pendingReward(address(0))` on each wired staker alongside the existing rewardToken() cross-check, so a shape mismatch reverts at deploy time rather than mid-migration.

findings.severityNote: NOT ESCALATED. Unreachable with phUSD (a standard bool-returning OZ ERC20, pinned by the constructor cross-check to the staker's own rewardToken) and weird-ERC20 behaviour is a C4 known-invalid class. Filed because it is a deviation from the code's OWN stated claim, and because it is the ONE place story-023 is materially weaker than the audit's run-20 candidate patch.
findings.specText: src/NFTStakerMigrator.sol:224-226 (identical at src/InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.sol:321-323): "Raw `transfer` inside `try`, NOT `safeTransfer`: SafeERC20 reverts rather than returning, which would defeat the `catch` on non-reverting-false tokens. Both branches are handled."
findings.actualBehavior: There is a THIRD branch the code does not handle: a token that returns NO data on success (the USDT/non-standard shape). `try rewardToken.transfer(user, captured) returns (bool ok)` must ABI-decode the return data; with empty return data that decode fails. The outcome is either (i) an uncaught revert that takes the whole batch down -- the exact failure mode the try/catch exists to prevent -- or (ii) if the failure lands in the catch, a DOUBLE-COUNT: the tokens have already left the contract, yet `unforwarded[user]` and `totalUnforwarded` are credited anyway (:236-237). Outcome (ii) is the worse one: `totalUnforwarded` then exceeds the held balance, so `rescueERC20`'s `balance - totalUnforwarded` (src/NFTStakerMigrator.sol:272, src/InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.sol:394) underflow-reverts permanently, and `claimForwarded()` pays out of other users' escrow.
findings.deviation: 'Both branches are handled' is a two-branch claim over a three-branch space. SafeERC20 handles all three correctly, which makes the deliberate choice to avoid it the source of the gap. test/MigratorRewardForwarding.t.sol covers the revert branch (testG) and the false-return branch (testG2); there is no no-return-data mock in the suite.
findings.recommendation: Either restrict the comment to the two branches actually handled, or wrap the raw call as a low-level `call` with explicit `returndata.length == 0 || abi.decode(returndata,(bool))` handling so the success-with-no-data case cannot escrow value that has already left.

findings.specText: src/NFTStakerMigrator.sol:70-76: "OFF-CHAIN RECONCILIATION CAVEAT. The staker still emits `Claimed(user, pending)` before the forward completes, so a settled payment can traverse TWO transfers (staker -> migrator -> user) under ONE `Claimed` event. Indexers keying on `Claimed` alone will mis-source the payment; join it with `RewardForwarded` / `RewardForwardFailed` from this contract to reconstruct the true flow. No on-chain change compensates for this."
findings.actualBehavior: The caveat is accurate but understates the escrow case. On the failure branch (src/NFTStakerMigrator.sol:231-238) `Claimed(user, X)` is on-chain and final while the user has received NOTHING and holds only an `unforwarded[user]` balance they must discover and claim themselves via `claimForwarded()`. There is no on-chain link from the Claimed event to the escrow, and no expiry, reminder, or owner-assisted delivery path.
findings.deviation: Disclosed, not hidden -- the story documents the two-transfer case explicitly. Filed as QA only because the disclosure covers the successful-forward case and not the escrowed case, where the accounting says paid and the user's balance says nothing, indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Extend the NatSpec caveat to name the escrow case, and surface `unforwarded[user]` in whatever UI reads Claimed.

findings.specText: story-022 stage 7 (commit fba4991 body): "This commit is a pure file/name split plus a verbatim restore -- no design change." and "docs/multi-token-nudge.md: Status flipped to implemented; contract references repointed at the sibling".
findings.actualBehavior: The literal `BatchNFTMinter` string references were correctly repointed (doc:1, 50, 240-245, 341) and none was left mis-pointing. But the doc's structure is a DELTA SPEC written against a contract being edited in place, and Stage 7 invalidated that framing without rewriting it. Concretely: doc:70-74 lists four items as '**Removed:**' (`nudgePaymentToken`, `setNudgePaymentToken`/`NudgePaymentTokenChanged`, `BatchMint__NudgeTokenMatchesPaymentToken`, the scalar `minReward`) -- all four are still live in the frozen contract at src/BatchNFTMinter.sol:87, 149-152, 111, 98, 242, because Stage 7 restored it byte-identical. Nothing was removed. doc:297-298 (§7 step 3) instructs 'remove `nudgePaymentToken` state + setter' -- actively wrong at HEAD. doc:353 (§8 acceptance check) predicts 'existing single-token nudge cases: +2-3k (the guard) and otherwise flat' -- unobservable, because post-split those cases run against the restored frozen contract which gained neither the guard nor `nonReentrant`, and snapshots/BatchNFTMinterTest.json was restored to its pre-story-022 shape. Six further implicit references still equivocate: doc:12-19 ('Today the nudge reward is a single ERC20...'), doc:109-111 ('the current contract'), doc:124-126 ('The existing single-token guard'), doc:160-162 ("Today's single-token design"), doc:214 ('Preserved from the current contract'), doc:314 ('where today it is O(1)').
findings.deviation: 'contract references repointed' was executed as a literal-string repoint only. The doc's every-behavioural-claim conformance against src/BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol is otherwise EXCELLENT (all of §2 signatures/errors, all ten §3 ordering steps, §4.1 unconditional exclusion, §4.2 four-site comment requirement, §4.3-§4.6, and all 21 named §6 tests verified CONFORMS) -- the defect is confined to the stale delta framing, which will mislead the next reader into believing the frozen contract was mutated.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite §2 and §7 from 'Removed/remove' to 'differs from the frozen `BatchNFTMinter` as follows', label every 'today'/'current contract' as the frozen sibling, and strike or restate the §8 acceptance check.

findings.specText: lib/phoenix-nft-staking/CLAUDE.md:44-45: "### Feature Specification (implementation checklist) -- Treat the list below as the authoritative spec. When the user asks for a new feature, cross-reference this list and remind them of any items still outstanding." and :47: "The emission model is the **variable-runway / owner-set APY target**". Also docs/multi-token-nudge.md:304 (§7 step 6): "Update `CLAUDE.md` if the nudge is described there."
findings.actualBehavior: The self-declared authoritative spec describes exactly ONE of the eleven files in src/. Items 1-10 (:49-77) and the Critical Invariants block (:52-67) pin `NFTStaker` semantics only (setTargetAPY, R = T*A/SECONDS_PER_YEAR, setStakedId, pullAndRefresh, ScheduleRecomputed). Not mentioned anywhere in CLAUDE.md: NFTStakerDepletion (a DIFFERENT emission model -- depletion window, not APY target -- and the one actually deployed to mainnet three times under phStaging story-071), NFTStakerPriceScaled, NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady, NFTStakerMigrator, InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator, BatchNFTMinter, BatchNFTMinterMultiToken, or any of the three interfaces. A case-insensitive grep of CLAUDE.md for batch|nudge|multi-token|depletion|pricescaled|migrator returns two hits, neither of which is a spec reference (:61 uses 'depletion' in its ordinary sense inside an NFTStaker invariant; :108 names the deleted deploy script). CLAUDE.md:47's assertion that 'The emission model is the variable-runway / owner-set APY target' is stated in the singular and is false of the mainnet staker.
findings.deviation: Stage 8 rewrote CLAUDE.md's project-structure section (accurately -- the 'NOT a deployment repo' block at :98-111 is fully verified: script/ is gone, nothing dangling references it, and the redirect to ../phase-2-staging is real) but left the authoritative spec covering 1 of 11 contracts. docs/multi-token-nudge.md:304 instructed 'Update CLAUDE.md if the nudge is described there' -- the conditional evaluated false, so the instruction terminated as a no-op and the multi-token nudge never entered the spec. Under Law 2 this matters directly: CLAUDE.md is a designated story source, so an agent or engineer 'cross-referencing this list' for a change to NFTStakerDepletion or either minter gets no acceptance criteria at all. Separately, Project Structure (:113-118) omits docs/, snapshots/, .gas-snapshot, and test/mocks/ (no phantom entries -- everything listed exists).
findings.recommendation: Extend the Feature Specification with a per-contract section for the depletion model, the two price-scaled variants, both migrators (including the settlement-capture forwarding contract from story-023), and both minters; or demote the section from 'authoritative spec' to 'NFTStaker reference' and point to docs/ for the rest.

findings.function: §1 'Why the honeypot framing does not apply'
findings.specText: docs/multi-token-nudge.md:42-46 at HEAD: "The pot is a *nudge*: by construction it is a fraction of the cost of the `nudgeSize` mints required to qualify. A bot that claims it must first pay more payment-token into the protocol than it extracts in reward. Every claim is net-positive for the protocol; there is no configuration of this mechanism under which claiming is profitable-in-isolation." Restated in code NatSpec at src/BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:56-61 and relied on again at docs/multi-token-nudge.md:232-233.
findings.specSource: docs/multi-token-nudge.md:42-46 (run-20 anchor was :41; Stage 7's header edit shifted it)
findings.actualBehavior: RE-DERIVED AT HEAD: the finding STILL STANDS, unchanged in substance and slightly strengthened. Stage 7 repointed the contract name at doc:50 but left the claim itself verbatim, and carried it into a NEW contract's NatSpec (src/BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:56-61). Exhaustive re-verification of BOTH files (read in full, plus a non-truncated grep of every comparison operator) confirms NO code enforces any ratio, cap, or value comparison between the nudge payout and what the batch paid. In BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol every comparison is: :352 a COUNT gate (`_nudgeSize != 0 && count >= _nudgeSize`), :363/:424/:454 loop bounds, :382/:384 payment-token dust/refund arithmetic, :431 `available < minReward` (a CALLER-protective minimum, never a protocol-protective maximum), :456 a zero skip. `paymentAmount` (:297, :357, :384, :386) never appears in an expression with `snapshot`, `available`, or any reward amount; `snapshot[i]` is written once (:434) and read once (:455). The contract never reads the dispatcher's price at all (only `primeToken()` at :322). Frozen BatchNFTMinter.sol: identical conclusion (`nudgeAmount` set to a raw full balance at :280, compared only to `minReward` at :296 and 0 at :300).
findings.deviation: The claim remains an off-chain funding-discipline property presented as a structural one, and it is load-bearing twice over (it is the stated reason 'the honeypot framing does not apply' at MT.sol:51-61, and the stated reason the §5 MEV posture is acceptable at doc:232-233). The doc contradicts itself three lines later at doc:48-50 ('If someone erroneously over-funds the contract... the error was in the sender'), which concedes the invariant is operator-maintained. Falsifiable from owner-reachable state alone: `setNudgeSize` (MT.sol:166-169) has no lower bound, so nudgeSize = 1 makes a single mint qualify for the entire balance of every listed token, while the pot side is permissionless and unbounded.
findings.recommendation: Unchanged from run-20: rewrite §1 to state the margin as an OPERATIONAL invariant that must be monitored, or enforce it in code. Keep routed to the spec-conformance report only -- the value impact remains fully accounted for in the existing nudge findings and filing it in the security stream would double-count.

findings.specText: story-022 stage 7 (commit fba4991 body): "src/BatchNFTMinter.sol -> src/BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol (contract and @title renamed; body untouched)".
findings.actualBehavior: src/BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:143 carries the revert string `"BatchNFTMinter: caller is not pauser"` -- it names the frozen sibling from inside the new contract, and is byte-identical to src/BatchNFTMinter.sol:119, so a `vm.expectRevert` cannot distinguish the two contracts.
findings.deviation: A faithful consequence of 'body untouched' (so arguably correct execution of the story), but the rename was explicitly in scope and this identifier was missed. Cosmetic; recorded so it is not later mistaken for evidence that the wrong contract was invoked.
findings.recommendation: Retarget the string in BatchNFTMinterMultiToken only; leave the frozen contract untouched.

findings.function: 'This is NOT a deployment or staging repo'
findings.specText: lib/phoenix-nft-staking/CLAUDE.md:105-107: "Deployment, wiring, address books and end-to-end staging live in **`../phase-2-staging`** (the `phStaging2` project). Send all deploy work there."
findings.actualBehavior: The redirect is sound for the FROZEN contract: lib/phoenix-phase-2-staging/script/MigrateBatchNFTMinter.s.sol:430 calls `setNudgePaymentToken(USDC)` and asserts it at :443 and :456, so review finding F2's root cause (a deploy path that omits nudgePaymentToken) verifiably does NOT exist in the real deployment repo -- deletion-rather-than-repair was safe. However, a grep of the entire phase-2-staging repo for `BatchNFTMinterMultiToken` returns ZERO hits. The contract that story-022 spent eight stages landing has no deployment path in this repo (forbidden) and none in the repo it redirects to.
findings.deviation: Not a defect in Stage 8 -- an undeployed new contract is a normal intermediate state -- but the combination of 'never add a deploy script here' with 'the staging repo has no support for this contract yet' means the newly landed feature is currently unreachable end-to-end. Recorded as a tracking note so it is not assumed shipped.
findings.recommendation: No change in this repo. Track a phStaging story to add BatchNFTMinterMultiToken deploy/wire support before the feature is considered delivered.

verifiedClaims.claim: story-023: 'the accrual depositFor settles is computed against the pre-pull budget -- exactly the quantity pendingReward(user) projects at the same timestamp', so require(captured <= owed) cannot fire on a legitimate migration.
verifiedClaims.evidence: src/NFTStakerDepletion.sol:423-435 runs _updatePool() at :424 BEFORE dispatcherHook.pull() at :429; _updatePool (:448-472) and pendingReward (:799-813) use identical inputs (same acc, rewardRate, windowEnd, rewardBudget cap, totalStaked guard) at the same block.timestamp. The settled `pending` at :754 therefore equals the pre-call projection exactly, and _safePayTo can only pay less (never more). The bound is fail-closed and cannot misfire.
